title: Timers: TON, TOF and TP
oneLiner: The three IEC timers as function blocks: on-delay, off-delay and pulse, their Q and elapsed time outputs, TIME literals, and the two rules that prevent most timer bugs.
keyTakeaway: TON: Q after IN has been TRUE for PT. TOF: Q with IN, held for PT after IN drops. TP: a fixed PT pulse from a rising edge. Call every timer once per scan, unconditionally, and expect the real delay to be PT rounded up to the next scan.
explanation:
Timers are function blocks: you declare an instance (a named copy with its own memory), call it every scan with its inputs, and read its outputs. IEC 61131-3 defines three. The on-delay timer TON turns its output Q on once its input IN has been TRUE for the preset time PT. The off-delay timer TOF turns Q on with IN and keeps it on for PT after IN goes off. The pulse timer TP turns Q on for exactly PT when IN rises, however long IN then stays on.

Each also has an elapsed time output, ET, which counts up while it is timing. Durations are TIME values, written as literals such as T#500ms, T#2s or T#1m30s.

A PLC timer isn't a separate clock interrupting the program. It checks the controller's clock each time the program calls it, so its output can only change when the program runs, once per scan. That has two practical effects: the real delay is PT rounded up to the next scan, and a timer the program stops calling stops updating.
